power_analysis_assumptions.sigma_label: REASONED WORKING ASSUMPTION, not measured -- see ASSUMED_SIGMA_PCT_OF_PREMIUM's docstring.
power_analysis_assumptions.cost_floor_label: COMPUTED from backtest.costs.DEFAULT_COST_MODEL.breakeven_move on an illustrative 150 premium / 65-qty round trip.
power_analysis_assumptions.recommended_effect_size_label: 2x the computed cost floor -- a reasoned 'modest edge worth having' threshold, not a sourced constant.
power_analysis_assumptions.iid_caveat: This is an i.i.d.-asymptotic power calculation. Real trade sequences have serial correlation / regime clustering (backtest/monte_carlo.py's own documented caveat: 'IID resampling destroys loss clustering, so these figures are optimistic'). The true required n is likely higher than computed here; this is a stated limitation, not corrected for by arbitrarily inflating the number.

reasoning_notes: Charter trade floor: leaderboard.MIN_TRADES_FOR_STATUS = 100 (also research.decision.decide's default min_trade_count and TradingMetrics.sufficient_sample's 100-trade floor -- three call sites agree on the same number).

Walk-forward window sizing (research.backtest.options_walk_forward.OptionsWalkForwardRequest defaults): train_bars=40, test_bars=20, step_bars=None -> effective step=20 (backtest.walk_forward.generate_windows treats a None step as test_bars, i.e. non-overlapping test slices).

backtest.walk_forward.MIN_OUT_OF_SAMPLE_TRADES = 100: the absolute out-of-sample trade floor a walk-forward verdict needs to pass (backtest.walk_forward._verdict), independent of the efficiency ratio.

MIN_WINDOWS_FOR_STABLE_READ = 6 (reasoned, by analogy to the ~5-fold floor commonly trusted in k-fold cross-validation): fewer windows than this and parameter_stability's per-parameter 'distinct'/'stable' counts and efficiency_ratio's average are themselves computed from too few points to trust -- backtest.walk_forward.parameter_sensitivity already refuses to assess anything from fewer than 3 parameter sets for the same reason, one level down.
That needs 160 bars structurally (generate_windows' own arithmetic, solved for 6 windows).

The options_walk_forward harness runs BuyAndHold per test window (one position opened and closed within the window), so it realizes roughly 1 trade per window -- not the many-trades-per-window a signal-based intraday strategy might produce. Reaching MIN_OUT_OF_SAMPLE_TRADES=100 combined out-of-sample trades on that path therefore needs on the order of 100 windows, i.e. 2040 bars -- far more than the 160-bar structural minimum for a stable efficiency-ratio read. This is a genuine finding, not a restatement: the two gates in backtest.walk_forward._verdict (efficiency ratio and the absolute OOS-trade floor) bind at very different bar counts for this specific (BuyAndHold-per-window) harness.

At 1-minute bars (375/session, from research.data.upstox.calendar.expected_bar_count against the real 375-minute NSE session), the binding 2040-bar requirement is ~6 trading days. At 5-minute bars (75/session), it is ~28 trading days.

A single weekly-expiry option contract only trades for roughly one week (~5 trading days) of its own life at meaningful liquidity, so the 5-minute-bar figure above (~28 days) cannot be satisfied from ONE contract's own history at all -- reaching the out-of-sample-trade floor requires pooling trades across many expiries/contracts (the same expiries this module is already sizing a backfill for), not extending a single contract's recorded window.

Regime context (research.regime.engine): RegimeDetector can assign 7 labels (['EVENT_RISK', 'HIGH_VOLATILITY', 'LOW_VOLATILITY', 'RANGE', 'TREND_DOWN', 'TREND_UP', 'UNKNOWN']), confirmed only after 3 consecutive matching raw readings (hysteresis). research.decision.decide's own min_regime_count default is 2 -- a conservative floor requiring only 2 of the 7 possible labels. Observing several of the substantive regimes (TREND_UP, TREND_DOWN, RANGE, HIGH_VOLATILITY, LOW_VOLATILITY -- excluding UNKNOWN and EVENT_RISK, which are refusal/override labels rather than market states) plausibly needs several months of calendar time, since NSE trend/volatility regimes typically persist for multiple weeks at a time -- this is a REASONED, not computed, claim.

Trading-days-per-year approximation: 250 (the standard ~52-week x 5-session-minus-holidays rule of thumb used across quantitative finance, cited as a well-known approximation, not measured from this project's own NSE holiday calendar).

Recommended min_trading_days = 250 (one full standard trading year): a pragmatic middle ground between the regime-diversity reasoning above and the much larger statistical-power-driven trade count computed in the power analysis below. This is stated explicitly as a floor, not a guarantee of adequacy -- see 'unverified_assumptions' and the power-analysis section for why the full recommended trade count likely needs more than one year of pooled history at realistic trade frequencies.

Expiry cadence verified live (web search, 2026-09-20): NIFTY weekly (Tuesday), BANKNIFTY monthly-only (weekly discontinued 1 Sep 2025), SENSEX weekly (Thursday) -- the Sep 2025 SEBI-mandated Tuesday/Thursday restructuring. This has changed by regulatory mandate multiple times in recent years and could change again; treated as current, not permanent.

min_distinct_expiries = 12: roughly one year of BANKNIFTY monthly expiries, or one quarter of NIFTY/SENSEX weeklies -- chosen so the floor is achievable for the slowest-cadence instrument within the same one-year window recommended above.

Strikes per expiry: ATM +/- 10 (21 strikes) -- REASONED, not sourced. research.strategies.option_selection.py implements ATM / ATM+1 / ATM-1 / DELTA *selection methods* but no fixed scan width; no other module in this project states a strike-count default.
Instruments: ['NIFTY', 'BANKNIFTY', 'SENSEX'] -- the project's own stated scope (UPSTOX_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md, core.upstox_instruments's NSE_INDEX/BSE_INDEX handling).

Row-count formula: min_trading_days x avg_listed_expiries_per_day (3, REASONED -- how many expiries a backfill tracks simultaneously per day, not the total distinct expiries occurring across the whole year, since any one expiry contract only trades during its own listed life) x strikes_per_expiry (21) x 2 (CE/PE) x bars_per_day x instruments (3).
At 1-minute bars: 250 x 3 x 21 x 2 x 375 x 3 = 35,437,500 rows (~11,828.5 MB at an estimated 350 bytes/row including both declared indexes).
At 5-minute bars: 250 x 3 x 21 x 2 x 75 x 3 = 7,087,500 rows (~2,365.7 MB).

Recommended interval: 5-minute bars (~5x cheaper in storage than 1-minute, while still fine-grained enough for the multi-bar-hold strategies this project's walk-forward path targets -- test_bars=20 at 5-minute bars already spans less than half an NSE session). 1-minute is noted as the alternative for a strategy that specifically needs sub-5-minute entry/exit precision.

Cost floor (COMPUTED): backtest.costs.DEFAULT_COST_MODEL.breakeven_move on an illustrative 150-premium / 65-qty round trip = 0.67% of premium. A trade's net return must clear this before any profit is real.

Return dispersion (REASONED, not measured): sigma = 30.0% of premium, taken from the illustrative 30-50% short-window premium swings in tests/research/test_option_economics_vs_direction.py's synthetic scenario. A real sigma must eventually come from real collected trades (the Upstox backfill this module's requirement feeds).

Power calculation: n = ((z_a/2 + z_b)^2 x sigma^2) / delta^2, with z_a/2=1.9600 (95% two-sided), z_b=0.8416 (80% power), sigma=30.0%. Results by candidate minimum effect size (delta, as % of premium): delta=0.5% -> n=28,256; delta=1.0% -> n=7,064; delta=2.0% -> n=1,766; delta=5.0% -> n=283; delta=10.0% -> n=71.
Recommended effect size = 1.34% (2x the computed cost floor) -> required n = 3,935.

COMPARISON: the charter's own MIN_TRADES_FOR_STATUS is 100. The power calculation above requires 3,935 trades to reliably (95% confidence, 80% power) distinguish a 1.34%-of-premium edge from noise at the assumed 30.0% dispersion. 100 trades is only adequate, by this same formula, for effect sizes at the very large end of the tested range (see required_n_by_effect_size_pct) -- the charter's 100-trade floor is a reasonable 'stop pretending you know anything below this' floor (and matches this project's own framing of it as exactly that: 'treat any metric here as indicative only'), but it is NOT, by this power calculation, adequate to reliably detect a modest, realistic post-cost edge. These two numbers disagree, and that disagreement is the intended finding of this analysis, not an error to reconcile.

Caveat (stated, not corrected for): this is an i.i.d.-asymptotic calculation. Real trade sequences cluster by regime (backtest/monte_carlo.py's own documented caveat about block-bootstrap vs IID resampling: 'IID resampling destroys loss clustering, so these figures are optimistic'). The true required n is likely higher than what is computed here.
unverified_assumptions: ASSUMED_SIGMA_PCT_OF_PREMIUM (30% per-trade return dispersion): a REASONED WORKING ASSUMPTION for sizing purposes, not measured from real trade data -- the project's real database is empty. Must be replaced by a measurement from real collected trades once available.
AVG_LISTED_EXPIRIES_PER_DAY = 3 (how many expiries a backfill tracks simultaneously per trading day): reasoned, not derived from any existing project constant or measurement.
STRIKES_PER_EXPIRY = 21 (ATM +/- 10): reasoned working range; no strategy generator in this codebase currently hardcodes a strike-count default.
ESTIMATED_BYTES_PER_ROW = 350: estimated from the `bars` table's column list in research/data/upstox/store.py, not measured against a populated database (the real store is empty).

The options_walk_forward harness realizing ~1 trade per test window (used to derive the OOS-trade-floor bar requirement): a reasoned inference from reading BuyAndHold's behavior in research/backtest/options_walk_forward.py, not an independently measured trade-frequency figure.

The i.i.d.-independence assumption underlying the entire power calculation in power_analysis_assumptions: documented as optimistic per backtest/monte_carlo.py's own caveat about serial correlation / loss clustering, not corrected for.

Expiry cadence (NIFTY weekly/BANKNIFTY monthly/SENSEX weekly): verified via a live web search on 2026-09-20 reflecting the Sep 2025 SEBI-mandated restructuring, but this cadence has changed by regulatory mandate multiple times in recent years and is not guaranteed to still hold at the time this module is read -- re-verify before relying on it for a live backfill plan.
